title: This Bird Sees Two Summers a Year, 44,000 Miles Apart

scenes.text: One bird sees more daylight than any other animal. It weighs about three and a half ounces.
The Arctic tern breeds near the North Pole, then flies to Antarctica. Then it flies back.
Tiny trackers showed the real trip: a zigzag of about forty-four thousand miles every year, stopping for a month mid-Atlantic.
Over a lifetime of around thirty years, that adds up to roughly three round trips to the Moon.
Two summers a year, and no winter at all. That's why it's said to see more daylight than any other animal.

subject: Arctic tern
description:
One bird sees more daylight than any other animal.
The Arctic tern flies from the Arctic to Antarctica and back, about 44,000 miles a year, chasing summer at both ends of the Earth.
Which animal's journey amazes you most?
